title: The open–closed triangle at every coefficient stage
statement:
Let $X$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme, let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be
a closed immersion and $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ the complementary open
immersion. Let $\Lambda$ be one of the coefficient stages
$A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\Qlb$, with the categories $D^b_c(-,\Lambda)$
([def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed],
[def-weil-rationalization-karoubi],
[def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]), the pullbacks $i^*,j^*$ of
[def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], the direct image $i_*=Ri_*$ of
[def-weil-derived-direct-image] and the extension by zero $j_!=Rj_!$ of
[def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support]. For
$K\in D^b_c(X,\Lambda)$ the open counit and the closed unit extend to a
distinguished triangle, the open–closed recollement triangle of
[def-weil-open-closed-recollement],
$$
j_!j^*K\longrightarrow K\longrightarrow i_*i^*K
\longrightarrow j_!j^*K[1].
$$
Moreover $\operatorname{Hom}(j_!j^*K[m],i_*i^*K)=0$ for all $m$; hence the
third arrow is uniquely determined by the other two and the triangle is
functorial in $K$. If $X=X_0\otimes_{k_0}k$, $Z$, $U$ come from
$k_0$-schemes, $\Lambda\in\{E,\Qlb\}$ and $K$ is a Weil complex
([def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]), then all three arrows are
Weil-equivariant.

proof.text: Finite type over a field makes X locally Noetherian, and quasi-compactness over Spec k makes X compact. The open immersion induces a Noetherian topology on U, hence is quasi-compact; composition gives its finite-type structure over k. Base change gives the analogous geometric-fibre Noetherian structure. At level n=m+1, use the ordinary triangle and the restriction/closed-image constructibility clauses of lem-sf-finite-kernel-constructible-localization. Transport tensor inverse image to the intrinsic pullback by def-trf-finite-pullback-coordinate-comparison. Exact open extension preserves constructibility and cohomological support. Exact closed direct image is its own right derived functor, so both outer vertices are constructible. Disjoint support makes closed restriction of open extension zero on every unbounded complex. The closed adjunction then kills Hom(open(K)[r],closed(L)) for every r and independent K,L. Triangle-morphism extension gives uniqueness of the final map and naturality for every middle map, with exactly the prescribed counit and unit.

source.place: Finite-stage ringed localization; integral coefficient comparison

proof.text: The completed coefficient comparison is the already stated PurCompactSupport.completedPullMap, so its isomorphism follows from def-pur-integral-compact-support-coefficient-data. For module exactness, apply ringed localization to the open complement of the closed immersion and the actual completed ring. The open counit is a pointwise kernel of the closed unit by exactness and monicity. Evaluation jointly reflects limits, giving a natural isomorphism of its composite with the kernel in the functor category. Transport the closed adjunction through the coefficient equivalence, using uniqueness of adjoints; the unit kernels are naturally isomorphic. Thus the specified kernel and closed composite inherit additivity and finite limits/colimits from the ringed exact functors. No integral constructibility claim is used in this sheaf-level argument.

source.place: Finite-stage ringed localization; integral coefficient comparison

proof.text: The remaining geometric lemma identifies the exact completed kernel and closed image with the recorded integral operations and proves integral constructibility and canonical linearity. It makes no triangle or Hom assertion.

source.place: Integral sheaf localization and coefficient passage, steps 3–10

proof.text: The pointwise completed sheaf sequence is short exact. Localize it termwise to obtain the actual prescribed unit and kernel inclusion. The closed adjunction has invertible counit, so exact localization orthogonality gives shifted cross-object Hom vanishing. Restrict to the full triangulated integral constructible subcategory. Triangle-morphism extension proves uniqueness of the connecting arrow and naturality for every middle map.

source.place: Integral sheaf localization and coefficient passage, steps 3–10

proof.text: Localize the integral presentation as before. The raw localization is exact and its Hom groups tensor the integral groups, giving the prescribed rational triangle and shifted vanishing. At every finite coefficient field apply sfOpenClosedTriangle_integral_rational; choose these finite presentations inside the theorem proof. Apply normalized common-stage descent to these presentations, then triangle_morphism_extension gives uniqueness of the connecting arrow and naturality for all common-stage maps.

source.place: Integral sheaf localization and coefficient passage, steps 3–10

proof.text: Geometric Frobenius commutes with $i,j$ by base change from $k_0$. The automorphism lemma supplies exact constructible equivalences at all four stages and the coherent pullback comparisons $b,d$, even for semilinear Frobenius.

source.place: Weil structures; original step 12 and compositors in 13

proof.text: For the qbar Weil clause, the automorphism theorem supplies a shift structure and exactness of the actual common-stage geometric Frobenius. Apply normalized common-stage descent to P,Q using the complementary open, obtaining cross-object shifted Hom vanishing. Literal object normalization transfers that vanishing to the given R. For an object K, use its own coefficient stage and the normalized rational triangle theorem; the exact stage inclusion and the two normalization isomorphisms transport the distinguished triangle to the prescribed maps of R. The common-stage square theorem supplies the two outer isomorphisms and first two squares. Apply the same triangle-morphism-extension helper as in the rational clause to obtain third-arrow equivariance and uniqueness of both outer structures.

source.place: Weil structures paragraph; common-stage coefficient passage

proof.text: For the rational Weil clause, the automorphism theorem supplies exactness and a shift structure on the actual geometric Frobenius functor. The normalized rational recollement theorem gives distinguished completions and all shifted cross-object vanishing. The normalized mate-square lemma gives the two outer isomorphisms and first two squares for every middle Weil pair. Map the triangle by exact Frobenius. Conjugating shifted vanishing by the open Weil isomorphism kills its extension obstruction. Triangle-morphism extension supplies the third square and uniqueness of each outer arrow. Iso.ext and Prod.ext give uniqueness of the pair of outer isomorphisms. The preceding step assembles the qbar clause with the same helper.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $X$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme, let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be
a closed immersion and $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ the complementary open
immersion. Let $\Lambda$ be one of the coefficient rings
$A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\Qlb$, regarded as condensed rings, with the categories
$D^b_c(-,\Lambda)\subseteq D(-_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$ of [def-sf-setting].
Use the pullbacks $i^*,j^*$ of $\Lambda$-modules, the direct image $i_*=Ri_*$
and the extension by zero $j_!$ ([det-def-sf-operations]). For
$K\in D^b_c(X,\Lambda)$ the open counit and the closed unit extend to a
distinguished triangle in $D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$, the open–closed
recollement triangle of [def-weil-open-closed-recollement],
$$
j_!j^*K\longrightarrow K\longrightarrow i_*i^*K
\longrightarrow j_!j^*K[1],
$$
all of whose vertices lie in $D^b_c(X,\Lambda)$.
Moreover $\operatorname{Hom}(j_!j^*K[m],i_*i^*K)=0$ for all $m$; hence the
third arrow is uniquely determined by the other two and the triangle is
functorial in $K$. If $X=X_0\otimes_{k_0}k$, $Z$, $U$ come from
$k_0$-schemes, $\Lambda\in\{E,\Qlb\}$ and $K$ is a Weil complex
([sk-def-sf-weil-complexes], [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]), then all three
arrows are Weil-equivariant.

proof.text:
*The triangle.* The argument is the same for every $\Lambda$. Apply
[sk-prop-sf-open-closed-triangle] with $B=\Lambda_X=p_X^*\Lambda$. Its inverse
images are $i^*\Lambda_X=\Lambda_Z$ and $j^*\Lambda_X=\Lambda_U$, since
pullback of the condensed ring commutes with inverse image along $i$ and $j$
([det-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]). The functors $i^*$, $i_*$, $j^*$,
$j_!$ on $\Lambda$-module sheaves are exact, so they act on complexes and pass
to derived categories without deriving. For a complex $M$ of
$\Lambda_X$-modules representing $K$, the termwise exact sequence

$$
0\longrightarrow j_!j^*M\longrightarrow M\longrightarrow i_*i^*M\longrightarrow0
$$

of [sk-prop-sf-open-closed-triangle] is a short exact sequence of complexes,
natural in $M$. It gives a distinguished triangle in
$D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$, whose first two arrows are the counit of
$j_!\dashv j^*$ and the unit of $i^*\dashv i_*$
([prop-weil-open-closed-recollement-adjunctions]).

*Hom vanishing.* Since $j_!\dashv j^*$ is an adjunction of exact functors, it
persists on derived categories. Moreover $j^*i_*=0$: for $V\to U$ weakly étale,
$(i_*N)(V)=N(V\times_XZ)=N(\varnothing)=0$. Hence
$\operatorname{Hom}(j_!N[m],i_*M)=\operatorname{Hom}(N[m],j^*i_*M)=0$. Two
completions of the first two arrows differ by an automorphism $h$ of the third
vertex with $h-\operatorname{id}$ factoring through $i_*i^*K\to
j_!j^*K[1]$, hence through a zero map; so $h=\operatorname{id}$. The same
vanishing gives functoriality.

*Constructibility.* The pullback $j^*$ is exact and preserves constructible
sheaves, so $j^*K\in D^b_c(U,\Lambda)$. Since $D^b_c(X,\Lambda)$ is a
triangulated subcategory ([det-def-sfb-bounded-constructible]), containing $K$,
it suffices to show $j_!j^*K\in D^b_c(X,\Lambda)$; then $i_*i^*K$ is in it
as well. For $\Lambda=\mathcal O_E$ this is [sk-lem-integral-models], (3). For
$\Lambda=E,\Qlb$ one has $D^b_c=D^b_{ctf}$, and $j_!=Rj_!$ preserves
$D^b_{ctf}$ ([sk-thm-existence], (2)). For $\Lambda=A=A_{E,n}$ use the
étale comparison of [def-sf-setting]. Write $K\cong\nu_X^*G$ with $G$ a
bounded constructible complex on the étale site
([lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin]); then $j_!j^{-1}G$ is bounded
constructible, since $j_!$ is exact and carries the constructible
cohomology sheaves of $j^{-1}G$ to constructible sheaves
([lem-fin-extension-by-zero];
[Tag 095X](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/095X)). The comparisons of
[lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison] (for $j_!$),
[lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback] (for $j^*,i^*$) and
[prop-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image] (for the finite, hence
quasi-compact, $i$), together with the exactness of $\nu_X^*$
([prop-weil-pbc-site-comparison-finite-level]), identify the triangle with
$\nu_X^*$ of the étale triangle $j_!j^{-1}G\to G\to i_*i^{-1}G\to$ of
[lem-cbc-open-closed-recollement].

*Weil structures.* The geometric Frobenius $g_X$ of
[def-weil-frobenius-detailed] restricts to $g_U$ and $g_Z$, and the squares
formed by $j$, $i$ and these automorphisms are cartesian. The exchange maps
of [fix-lem-exchanges] for these automorphism squares are isomorphisms
(their inverses come from the inverse squares), and they give the Weil
structures on $j_!$ and $i_*$; the pullbacks use $g_U^*j^*=j^*g_X^*$ and
$g_Z^*i^*=i^*g_X^*$. The counit and unit are equivariant, since the exchange
maps are built from, and paste with, the same units and counits
([fix-lem-exchanges]). Transporting the triangle along $g_X^*$ and the Weil
isomorphisms gives a distinguished triangle with the same first two arrows;
by the uniqueness above it has the same third arrow, which is therefore
equivariant.
